newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - June 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - June 30.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Monday's Daily Variety:
* Paramount's thriller, "Face/Off" brought in a projected $22.7 million in its weekend opening, edging out Disney's animated "Hercules," which took in an estimated $21.5 million.
* General Electric's NBC is close to deals to score an unprecedented eight-year sponsorship pacts for five consecutive Olympics through 2008.

* John Singleton's remake of Shafthas been moved out of MGM, which is co-owned by billionaire investor Kirk Kerkorian's Tracinda Corp and Australian media company Seven Network Ltd, and set up at Paramount Pictures with Scott Rudin producing, sources said.
* Writer-director Jonathan Mostow has signed a deal at Seagram's Universal to direct as well as produce movies.
* MGM's Leo the Lion is, for the seventh time in the last 50 years, quietly re-inventing himself from scratch.
* Boxer Mike Tyson's bite out of rival Evander Holyfield's ear could actually increase his marketability in the pay-per-view arena, if he's not banned from boxing.
